sections.title: IMPORTANT - DELOAD/TRANSITION WEEK
sections.description:
Hi Team,

We’re wrapping up our current training block this week.

Week 4/4 will be what I call a transition week.

What does that mean? After three weeks of rigid, structured progressions, we're going to change things up. We do so in order to balance the rigidity and flexibility that make up a great training program for CrossFit. 
Too much structure and set systems has its limitations, just as too much variance and chaos does.
For us, based on the last 11 years of programming/training/coaching, we've found a 3-week "on" / 1-week "off" routine to be the most effective way to balance out the above.

This transition week looks very different to how we normally build the training programs, so if you are new to the team, please keep that in mind.

There will be less training overall this week to allow for better quality and better recovery, so that you are ready for a new training week starting next Monday.
 
Intensity is self-regulated. If you feel great, push. If you don’t, dial it back.
_______________________
Monday 20th of July we start fresh and continue our progressive overload. I can’t wait to show you what’s coming.
– André Houdet
nst

sections.title: CURRENT TRAINING BLOCK W4/4
sections.description:
Welcome to week 4 of our current training block Team,
If you just joined the team, make sure to read below:

I encourage you to watch the block explanation video below that will give you a deep insight into how the program is structured from a macro to micro level (Global-->Weekly-->Daily overview). 
Video link (block explanation): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gTI0JK4CSTU

If you do not have the time to watch the block explanation video, you can as always read the detailed notes attached in each section of the program to understand the intent behind everything. Due to FITr's layout, we have added the text as attachments to have less text in each box.

Our goal with this training program is to have you feel:
a. Constant progress through consistent good training weeks.
b. Feeling good (injury free)
c. Motivated and driven as you see and understand the intention of how the program is structured.

Our training principles to have success with the program:
#1 If you want to be good at something, you must above all else,
be consistent.
#2 Minimum Effective dose: This is a principle that we use to underline the concept of more frequent good training sessions leads to better results long term. Often if we train too hard we also need a longer recovery time before we can train hard again. Rather keep 5% in the tank instead of overreaching. Typically, people who do not take the needed recovery time from the sessions where they did more than they should end up injured/hits a plateau. We do not need to go to the maximum every time to create adaptation. 
#3 Self-regulation: Listen to your body and adjust the intensity based on how you feel.
#4 Consistently good rather than occasionally great: Many good sessions are always better than a few great. 
#5 The devil is in the detail: Be deliberate and pay attention to set up/reps/tempo/intensity described in the program. 
#6 Stay in your lane: Don’t get caught up in anybody else’s game, you focus on you and your progress.
#7 Technique > Load
#8 Quality > Quantity
#9 Principles > Methods
--------------------------------------
Have a great training block team,
/𝙰𝚗𝚍𝚛𝚎 𝙷𝚘𝚞𝚍𝚎𝚝
𝙳𝚒𝚛𝚎𝚌𝚝𝚘𝚛 𝚘𝚏 𝚃𝚛𝚊𝚒𝚗𝚒𝚗𝚐.
𝚗𝚜𝚝.

sections.title: WARM UP
sections.description:
Weightlifting, Warm up 

a. Pulsed stretches
1 round of:
60/60 sec Dynamic Pec Stretch
60/60 sec Dynamic Lat Stretch
60/60 sec Dynamic Anterior Hip stretch
60/60 sec Dynamic Posterior Hip stretch
20 Calf raises (10 Straight legs/10 bent legs)

b. Activation 
1-2 rounds of:
Mini-band squat prep routine (3x5 Iso squat hold + 5 air squat, 3x5 Iso glute bridge hold + 5 glute bridges)
15 Empty barbell goodmornings
5 x 1 Low ceiling jump squat + 2 Alt. Low ceiling split squat jumps

c. Weightlifting, Cleans specific barbell prep (Empty barbell)
5 Clean Pulls from above knees
-Rest as needed-
5 Muscle Cleans from above knees
-Rest as needed-
5 Power Cleans from above knees
-Rest as needed-
5 Squat Cleans from above knees
-Rest as needed-
Repeat with 3 reps at 40/25kg │ 95/65lbs

d. DU / Clean specific prep:
Build to the starting load for the Hang Clean piece (60% of your 1RM clean=@60%1RM_CLEAN). 
Between every build up set, hit a set of 20-30 Single or Double unders.

attachments.title: Posterior box hip stretch with reaches
Low ceiling jump squat + jump split squat complex
Mini band routine (iso hold + squat, iso hold + glute bridge)

sections.title: POWER/SPEED STRENGTH (Cleans)
sections.description:
Power/Speed strength, Cleans

a. Every 90 sec until you've reach a technical max
50 Double Unders* + 1 Hang Squat Clean 

Load: Start at 60% of your 1RM clean (@60%1RM_CLEAN) and add 2.5kg to each side every set

Technical max: Stop when form breaks down. 

*RX: 40 reps
*Intermediate: 30 reps

sections.title: CONDITIONING #2
sections.description:
Conditioning

Note: The Seated Ring Muscle-ups below can be quite difficult, so I've added lots of banded and non-banded options for you. However, if you'd rather just do regular RMU/BMU/Pull-ups+Dips, that modification is also completely fine for today. Enjoy!

Elite 
a. 10 rounds for time:
10/8 Cal Echo bike
2 Seated Strict Ring Muscle up
3 Box Jumps (40/30”) (no rebound)

RX
a. 10 rounds for time:
10/8 Cal Echo bike
2 Seated Banded Strict Ring Muscle up (3 Different band set ups to try)
3 Box Jumps (30/24”) (no rebound)

Intermediate
Option #1
a. 10 rounds for time:
10/8 Cal Echo bike
2 Strict Ring Muscle ups with feet on floor
3 Box Jumps (24/20”) (no rebound)

Option #2
a. 10 rounds for time:
10/8 Cal Echo bike
3 Strict Pull ups + 3 Ring Push ups
3 Box Jumps (24/20”) (no rebound)

Score: Time. (make sure to put a comment with what level you completed it at)
